label: input c at original position 3-4
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter c during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, almost entirely at positions t=3 and t=4 (99% of activation mass). Every c at t=3 or t=4 activates it (precision 1.0 on dev). Weak tail activations (around 0.05-0.2 of max) occur for c at t=2 and t=5; never fires at t=0,1 or t>=6, never on any other token, and never in the delimiter or copy phase (even when c is fed back as input). Magnitude is highest at t=3 (top examples ~0.98 of max) and somewhat lower at t=4 (~0.7-0.85); repeated or non-first occurrences of c appear to be somewhat weaker. Insensitive to L, the previous tokens, and the first token.

issues: Minor factual error in the hedged aside: a repeated c at t=3/4 is not weaker. The (in_first==0) subset has mass share / count of about 3.37e-5, against about 3.33e-5 for all c at t=3/4. The lower firing rate for in_first=0 in the profile comes from position (repeats tend to occur later in the sequence), not from repetition. The explanation already flagged this as unchecked.

The weak t=2 and t=5 tail is partial: only about 9% of c at t=2 or t=5 fire (precision 0.092, recall 0.079, mass 0.9%). None of the splits I tried give it structure: prev_tok a digit 0.071, L<=4 0.087, L>=8 at t=5 0.097, prev_tok c 0.091. It looks like scattered low-magnitude noise, not a systematic missed class.

The other claims hold on dev. There are 0 activations in the delimiter or copy phase, and c in phase!=0 has precision 0 over 90k steps. Firing is 0 at t=0, t=1 and t>=6. c is the only token that fires. t=3 alone and t=4 alone each have precision 1.0, and t=3 has higher mean magnitude than t=4 (about 12% higher). Test: precision 1.000, recall 0.917, F1 0.957, mass recall 0.991, and test misses show 0 false positives.

The lower firing rate at L=3 and L=4 has a structural cause, not an L effect: when L=3 there is no original step at t=3 or t=4, and when L=4 there is none at t=4. That fits the explanation's claim that L does not matter.
